decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 4.25% to 4.5%. The vote was 9-2. Dissenting: Michelle W. Bowman, Christopher J. Waller.

changes.quote: Although swings in net exports continue to affect the data, recent indicators suggest that growth of economic activity moderated in the first half of the year.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Although swings in net exports have affected the data, recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace.”

changes.quote: Uncertainty about the economic outlook remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Uncertainty about the economic outlook has diminished but remains elevated.”

changes.quote: Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Alberto G. Musalem; and Jeffrey R. Schmid.

changes.quote: Voting against this action were Michelle W. Bowman and Christopher J. Waller, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Absent and not voting was Adriana D. Kugler.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities.

The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments.
Although swings in net exports continue to affect the data, recent indicators suggest that growth of economic activity moderated in the first half of the year.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.37% APR costs about $89.04 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.38% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.75% would rise by about $7.98 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 34k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.7% over the past year (June 2025); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +8 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.12%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.36% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 57%, cut 43%, hike 0%.

citations.detail: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.
